- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >10% above recent mean), reduce by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is significantly below recent 18-day average, adjust upward by 2–5% to align with mean reversion bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from forecast in first 5–7 days, apply “early correction” by adjusting first 3–5 points toward true trend.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
